samples.summary: `DocStore.applyCellStyle` interface contract still documents the pre-change behaviour ("undefined will not remove it"), which `YorkieDocStore` now violates
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:117-118 declares: "Apply partial cell style … Additive only — setting a property to undefined will not remove it from the tree." The diff makes `YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2452-2470, via the new `removedCellStyleAttrs` + `removeNodeStyle`) do exactly the removal the interface promises never happens, and the docs table context menu now depends on that removal (`applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: undefined })`, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230). Any other implementor/caller reading this contract (e.g. `MemDocStore.applyCellStyle`, packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:278-284, which only spreads and therefore leaves a present-but-undefined key rather than deleting one) is now inconsistent with the CRDT store. Fix belongs on the interface doc (and ideally on MemDocStore) rather than on the new code.

samples.summary: `MemDocStore.setBlockType` still injects a placeholder inline for a `table` block, breaking the "a table block's inlines is always []" invariant the new YorkieDocStore branch relies on
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:260-264 keeps `else if (block.inlines.length === 0) { block.inlines = [{ text: '', style: {} }]; }` with no `type !== 'table'` exclusion, while the diff adds exactly that exclusion to both the CRDT write and the cache update in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts (~1466 and ~1491) and justifies it by asserting `block.inlines` is always `[]` for a table. `Doc.setBlockType` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:394-403) routes to whichever store is installed, so a MemDocStore-backed document (CLI, docs harness, docs tests) produces a table block whose `inlines` is non-empty — the same model shape the Yorkie path now deliberately refuses to create, and the shape the new PUT validator treats as table-typed (`assertValidBlock` returns before the inlines check for tables). The two store implementations now disagree on the invariant.
searchedFor: read yorkie-doc-store setBlockType hunks in the diff

samples.summary: `PRST_BY_KIND` allowlist is not exhaustiveness-checked against `ShapeKind`, so any kind omitted now (or added later) silently exports as `rect` for every consumer of `kindToPrst`
samples.evidence: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts:19-95 builds the map from a hand-written literal typed `as const satisfies readonly Exclude<ShapeKind,'freeform'>[]`. `satisfies` only proves each listed string IS a ShapeKind; it does not prove the list COVERS the union, so a `ShapeKind` added to packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:54-125 (or one accidentally left out today) compiles cleanly and then degrades to `prst="rect"` at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts:96 — silent geometry loss in every exported .pptx, with no type error and no test that enumerates the union (packages/slides/test/export/pptx/shape.test.ts only spot-checks four kinds). A `Record<Exclude<ShapeKind,'freeform'>, string>` seed (or a test iterating the union) would make the map's completeness enforced rather than assumed.
